claim: TopoRadar-Net achieves competitive cross-system generalization on unseen mountain systems, achieving 77.40% +- 1.86% F1 and 63.16% +- 2.45% IoU on the Scandinavian Arctic benchmark (Tromso) and 50.18% +- 4.40% F1 on the Pamir Mountains (Pish, Tajikistan), with a pooled macro F1 of 63.79% +- 1.88% across three independent training seeds.

Reference benchmark Attention U-Net achieves 78.09% +- 0.99% F1 and 64.07% +- 1.33% IoU on the Scandinavian Arctic benchmark and 48.73% +- 2.74% F1 on the Pamir Mountains, with a pooled macro F1 of 63.41% +- 1.03% across three independent training seeds.
Deep ResU-Net baseline achieves 76.60% +- 1.30% F1 on the Scandinavian Arctic and 49.25% +- 3.39% F1 on the Pamir Mountains, with a pooled macro F1 of 62.92% +- 1.42% across three independent seeds.
Siamese differential U-Net baseline achieves 72.64% +- 0.39% F1 on the Scandinavian Arctic and 37.11% +- 2.44% F1 on the Pamir Mountains across three independent seeds.
Siamese concatenated U-Net baseline achieves 78.92% +- 1.07% F1 on the Scandinavian Arctic and 47.34% +- 0.70% F1 on the Pamir Mountains across three independent seeds.

Across 1,000 paired cluster-bootstrap draws over spatial test blocks (Seed 42), TopoRadar-Net achieves a statistically confirmed F1 gain of +2.30% (95% CI: [+0.27%, +4.41%], p = 0.030) over Attention U-Net on the Scandinavian Arctic benchmark.

Across 1,000 paired cluster-bootstrap draws over spatial test blocks (Seed 42), TopoRadar-Net achieves a statistically confirmed F1 gain of +4.35% (95% CI: [+1.33%, +7.38%], p = 0.010) over ResU-Net on the Scandinavian Arctic benchmark.

The paired 339-block spatial bootstrap versus Attention U-Net yields pooled micro-F1 differences of +3.26%, -2.99%, and +4.16% for Seeds 42, 123, and 456 (descriptive mean +1.48% +- 3.18%; positive in two of three seeds). Under 3-seed macro-F1 paired t-testing, only the difference versus SiamUNet-diff is significant (+8.92%, p = 0.021); competitive deep baselines remain statistically indistinguishable across seeds.

Exploratory Seed-42 backslope differences versus Attention U-Net (+5.85% F1 in Tromso; +5.09% in Pamir) do not persist as stable three-seed effects. Full-scene multi-seed mean differences are -0.34% +- 6.28% and +1.20% +- 7.73%, respectively, with positive differences in two of three seeds per region. These descriptive associations do not isolate a causal mechanism.

At 30% area overlap, TopoRadar-Net achieves an overall hit rate of 75.50% +- 1.61% on Tromso (88.3/117 mean detected polygons), detecting 100% of Class D4 avalanches in 2 of 3 seeds (mean 95.8%) and 84.0% of Class D3 avalanches.

Omitting local incidence angle conditioning (No-LIA) is associated with -1.73% Tromso pixel F1 (77.40% versus 75.67%) and a paired cluster-bootstrap difference of -2.04% (95% CI: [-3.13%, -0.98%], p < 0.001). This component-removal result establishes sensitivity, not a causal normalization mechanism.

Geo-Loss is a heuristic slope prior with a positive-label conflict: its mask contains 18.47% of training positives. Removing it changes Tromso precision from 75.48% to 72.50% and yields a Seed-42 paired-cluster F1 difference of -3.16% (No-GeoLoss minus full; p = 0.002), while increasing three-seed held-out positive recall inside the penalty mask in Tromso (50.47% to 71.29%) and Pamir (1.08% to 6.45%). This is a precision-recall trade-off, not a physical-admissibility mechanism.

Multi-region ablation records regime-dependent sensitivity: the full configuration is stronger in Tromso under selected comparisons, whereas simpler representations attain higher Pamir F1 (53.30% versus 50.18%), and No-Aspect/No-CrossAttn exceed the full model on pooled macro F1.

Proposition 2 characterizes the geometric limitations of shift-invariant 2D linear spatial convolutions across opposing mountain facets under non-stationary radiometric projection and motivates continuous orientation coordinates without circular angular branch cuts.

claim: Evaluating on the polar maritime validation cohort (129 polygons, 81,595 debris pixels), TopoRadar-Net achieves highest sensitivity (81.50% +- 1.10% recall) and 66.75% +- 1.96% F1, clustering within 0.41% of Attention U-Net (67.01% +- 1.98%) and ResU-Net (67.16% +- 1.62%), honestly corroborating regime-dependent sensitivity in moderate-relief sub-polar terrain.

On affine-transform valid-mask areas of 196.820 km2 (Tromso) and 267.435 km2 (Pish), TopoRadar-Net records false-positive footprints of 74.77 and 129.69 ha (0.38 and 0.48 ha/km2). Relative to the bottleneck self-attention U-Net, this is a 30.0% Pish reduction (55.63 ha) but a 28.5% Tromso increase (16.58 ha); Class D4 completeness in Tromso is 95.8%.

In a post-hoc exploratory proxy using validation-only Platt calibration and F2 threshold selection, TopoRadar-Net corridor alerts in Pamir achieve 83.02% +- 2.34% precision and 62.50% +- 10.21% recall across three seeds; all seeds miss the single Tromso corridor-intersecting component. All cached end-to-end TopoRadar scene runs remain below 5 seconds on the profiled Apple MPS environment. This is not stakeholder or dispatch validation.
